title: Article 126 — Appointment of acting Chief Justice

content.overview: Article 126 provides that when the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant, or when the Chief Justice is, by reason of absence or otherwise, unable to perform the duties of the office, the duties of the office shall be performed by such one of the other Judges of the Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.
content.glance: CJI office vacant or CJI unable: President appoints another SC Judge to perform duties of CJI.
content.study:
Article 126 ensures continuity in the office of Chief Justice of India. The President appoints one of the other Judges of the Supreme Court to perform the duties when the office is vacant or the CJI is unable to perform them.

Examination: vacancy or inability; President appoints another SC Judge.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: When the office of CJI is vacant, or the CJI is unable to perform duties (absence or otherwise), the President may appoint one of the other Judges of the Supreme Court to perform the duties of the office.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who acts when the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 126, when the office of Chief Justice of India is vacant or the Chief Justice is unable to perform the duties of the office by reason of absence or otherwise, the duties are performed by such one of the other Judges of the Supreme Court as the President may appoint for the purpose.

examTips: President appoints another SC Judge as acting CJI.

keyTakeaways: Art 126: acting Chief Justice appointed by President from other SC Judges.
